title: 263. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Polynomial End Behavior from Leading Terms
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Identifying the Leading Term of a Polynomial
questions.learningObjective: Identify the leading term of a polynomial written in standard form.
questions.question: For the polynomial \(f(x)=-3x^4+2x^3-7x+1\), what is the leading term?
questions.explanation: The leading term of a polynomial is the term containing the highest power of \(x\). In \(f(x)=-3x^4+2x^3-7x+1\), the highest power is \(x^4\), so the leading term is \(-3x^4\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Look for the term with the greatest exponent on \(x\).

questions.concept: End Behavior of an Even-Degree Polynomial with Positive Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the end behavior of a polynomial from its leading term.
questions.question: Which statement describes the end behavior of \(y=2x^6-5x^2+1\)?
questions.explanation: The leading term is \(2x^6\). The degree \(6\) is even, and the leading coefficient \(2\) is positive. For an even-degree polynomial with a positive leading coefficient, both ends of the graph point upward. Therefore both ends go to \(\infty\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Use the degree parity and the sign of the leading coefficient.

questions.concept: End Behavior of an Odd-Degree Polynomial with Negative Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the end behavior of a polynomial with odd degree and negative leading coefficient.
questions.question: Which statement describes the end behavior of \(y=-x^5+4x^3-2\)?
questions.explanation: The leading term is \(-x^5\). The degree \(5\) is odd, and the leading coefficient \(-1\) is negative. For an odd-degree polynomial with a negative leading coefficient, the right end goes down and the left end goes up. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: The degree tells you whether the ends match; the sign of the leading coefficient tells you which way the right end points.

questions.concept: Identifying a Polynomial from Its End Behavior
questions.learningObjective: Select the polynomial whose graph has a given end behavior.
questions.question: Which polynomial has a left end pointing down and a right end pointing up?
questions.explanation: A graph with left end down and right end up corresponds to an odd-degree polynomial with a positive leading coefficient. In \(y=x^3-4x\), the leading term is \(x^3\), so the degree is odd and the leading coefficient is positive. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check the degree parity and the sign of the leading coefficient.

questions.concept: Matching End Behavior to a Possible Leading Term
questions.learningObjective: Select a leading term that produces a given end behavior.
questions.question: A polynomial graph has its left end pointing up and its right end pointing down. Which leading term could produce this end behavior?
questions.explanation: Left end up and right end down means the polynomial has odd degree and a negative leading coefficient. The term \(-2x^3\) has odd degree \(3\) and negative coefficient \(-2\), so it can produce this end behavior. The term \(3x^5\) has odd degree but positive coefficient, which would give left end down and right end up. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: The degree tells you whether the ends match; the sign of the leading coefficient tells you which way the right end points.

questions.concept: End Behavior of an Even-Degree Polynomial with Negative Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the end behavior of a polynomial with even degree and negative leading coefficient.
questions.question: What is the end behavior of \(f(x)=-2x^4+3x^3-x\)?
questions.explanation: The leading term is \(-2x^4\). The degree \(4\) is even, and the leading coefficient \(-2\) is negative. For an even-degree polynomial with a negative leading coefficient, both ends of the graph point downward. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: The degree tells you whether the ends match; the sign of the leading coefficient tells you which way the right end points.

questions.concept: Inferring Leading Term Properties from End Behavior
questions.learningObjective: Infer degree parity and leading coefficient sign from a graph's end behavior.
questions.question: A polynomial has both ends pointing down. Which statement about its leading term is necessarily true?

options.label: A
options.text: The degree is even and the leading coefficient is negative.

options.label: B
options.text: The degree is odd and the leading coefficient is negative.

questions.explanation: If both ends of a polynomial graph point down, then as \(x\to\pm\infty\), the output goes to \(-\infty\). This happens when the degree is even and the leading coefficient is negative. An odd degree with a negative leading coefficient would have one end up and one end down. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Both ends in the same direction indicate an even degree.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which polynomial has the same end behavior as a given polynomial.
questions.question: Which polynomial has the same end behavior as \(y=3x^4-x+2\)?
questions.explanation: The leading term of \(y=3x^4-x+2\) is \(3x^4\). It has even degree \(4\) and positive leading coefficient, so both ends point upward. The polynomial \(y=5x^2+2x\) has leading term \(5x^2\), also even degree with positive leading coefficient, so both ends point upward. The polynomial \(y=-2x^4+1\) has even degree but negative leading coefficient, so both ends point downward. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the degree parity and the sign of the leading coefficient.

questions.concept: End Behavior from Degree and Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the correct end behavior for an odd-degree polynomial with negative leading coefficient.
questions.question: If a polynomial has odd degree and negative leading coefficient, which end behavior is correct?
questions.explanation: For an odd-degree polynomial with a negative leading coefficient, the graph falls to the right and rises to the left. Thus as \(x\to\infty\), \(f(x)\to-\infty\), and as \(x\to-\infty\), \(f(x)\to\infty\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: The degree tells you whether the ends match; the sign of the leading coefficient tells you which way the right end points.

questions.concept: End Behavior of a Factored Polynomial
questions.learningObjective: Determine the end behavior of a polynomial given in factored form.
questions.question: What is the end behavior of \(f(x)=(x-2)^3(x+1)^2\)?
questions.explanation: The leading term comes from the highest powers in each factor: \(x^3\cdot x^2=x^5\). So the polynomial has odd degree \(5\) and positive leading coefficient. For an odd-degree polynomial with a positive leading coefficient, the left end points down and the right end points up. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Multiply the highest powers from each factor to find the leading term.
